strings.d1.s0.name: Kiyomizu-dera
strings.d1.s0.tips: Wooden terrace on a 778 temple; empty at 08:00, three streams of Otowa waterfall, night openings in autumn and spring.
strings.d1.s1.name: Sannenzaka & Ninenzaka
strings.d1.s1.tips: Preserved stone-stepped lanes; tatami Starbucks, yatsuhashi (cinnamon sweet) tasting.
strings.d1.s2.name: Kodai-ji
strings.d1.s2.tips: Zen garden and bamboo; the temple of Hideyoshi's widow.
strings.d1.s3.name: Nishiki Market
strings.d1.s3.tips: 'Kyoto's Kitchen', a 400-year-old market; tamagoyaki, yuba, pickles. No eating while walking. Two streets.
strings.d1.s4.name: Gion Hanamikoji
strings.d1.s4.tips: Geisha district; Shirakawa canal, maiko head to work between 17:30 and 18:00 (photo rules apply, private lanes off limits).
strings.d1.b0.name: Omen Nishiki
strings.d1.b1.name: Yasaka Shrine
strings.d1.b1.tips: Gion's shrine and Maruyama Park; lanterns at night.
strings.d2.s0.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
strings.d2.s0.tips: 10,000 red torii; empty at 07:00, 45 minutes to the Yotsutsuji viewpoint (full loop 2.5 hours), open 24 hours.
strings.d2.s1.name: Byodo-in Uji
strings.d2.s1.tips: The Phoenix Hall from the 10 yen coin; 15 minutes on the JR Nara line, museum included.
strings.d2.s2.name: Nakamura Tokichi Uji
strings.d2.s2.tips: 1854 tea house; matcha soba and parfait, expect a queue, Uji matcha tasting.
strings.d2.s3.name: Uji River & Ujigami Shrine
strings.d2.s3.tips: Japan's oldest shrine and the riverside; tea shops.
strings.d2.s4.name: Fushimi Sake District Gekkeikan
strings.d2.s4.tips: Sake breweries along the canal; Gekkeikan Okura Museum, 3 tastings.
strings.d2.b0.name: Tofuku-ji
strings.d2.b0.tips: Zen garden and Tsutenkyo Bridge (autumn); instead of Uji.
strings.d2.b1.name: Tsuen Tea Uji
strings.d2.b1.tips: The world's oldest tea house, since 1160; at the foot of the bridge.
strings.d3.s0.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
strings.d3.s0.tips: Bamboo corridor; crowded after 08:00, enter via the north gate of Tenryu-ji.
strings.d3.s1.name: Tenryu-ji
strings.d3.s1.tips: UNESCO Zen temple; Sogenchi garden and borrowed mountain scenery.
strings.d3.s2.name: Togetsukyo Bridge & Katsura River
strings.d3.s2.tips: The Moon Crossing Bridge; boats, cherry and maple hills.
strings.d3.s3.name: Arashiyama Yoshimura Soba
strings.d3.s3.tips: Soba with a bridge view; tempura.
strings.d3.s4.name: Iwatayama Monkey Park
strings.d3.s4.tips: Macaque monkeys on a hilltop; 20-minute climb, city views.
strings.d3.b0.name: Sagano Romantic Train
strings.d3.b0.tips: Train through the Hozugawa valley; Torokko Saga, instead of the monkeys (stunning in autumn).
strings.d3.b1.name: % Arabica Arashiyama
strings.d4.s0.name: Kinkaku-ji
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Golden Pavilion; opens at 09:00, reflection in the pond, 30-minute loop.
strings.d4.s1.name: Ryoan-ji
strings.d4.s1.tips: Zen garden of 15 stones; sit quietly and you will see 14 of them.
strings.d4.s2.name: Ninna-ji
strings.d4.s2.tips: Five-storey pagoda and the late-blooming Omuro cherry (April).
strings.d4.s3.name: Nijo Castle
strings.d4.s3.tips: Shogun's palace; the 'nightingale floors' squeak, Ninomaru garden, closed Tuesdays (some months).
strings.d4.s4.name: Honke Owariya
strings.d4.b0.name: Ippudo Nishiki
strings.d4.b1.name: Kyoto Imperial Palace
strings.d4.b1.tips: Imperial palace; free, instead of Nijo (closed Mondays).
strings.d5.s0.name: Nara Park Deer
strings.d5.s0.tips: 35 minutes on the Kintetsu line (direct from Kyoto); 1,200 free-roaming deer, shika senbei (deer crackers) 200 yen, they bow to greet you.
strings.d5.s1.name: Todai-ji Daibutsu
strings.d5.s1.tips: 15 m bronze Buddha; the world's largest wooden building, pillar hole.
strings.d5.s2.name: Kasuga Taisha
strings.d5.s2.tips: Path of 3,000 stone lanterns; in the forest.
strings.d5.s3.name: Nakatanidou Mochi
strings.d5.s3.tips: Lightning-fast mochi pounding show; yomogi (mugwort) mochi.
strings.d5.s4.name: Naramachi
strings.d5.s4.tips: Old merchant quarter; Koshi-no-ie house, cafes.
strings.d5.b0.name: Kamameshi Shizuka Nara
strings.d5.b0.tips: Pot rice (kamameshi); next to the park.
strings.d5.b1.name: Isuien Garden
strings.d5.b1.tips: Garden that borrows Todai-ji as scenery; instead of Naramachi.
strings.d6.s0.name: Ginkaku-ji
strings.d6.s0.tips: The Silver Pavilion (not actually silver); sand cone and moss garden.
strings.d6.s1.name: Philosopher's Path
strings.d6.s1.tips: 2 km canal path; cherry blossom in April, maple in November, cats.
strings.d6.s2.name: Nanzen-ji
strings.d6.s2.tips: Aqueduct (Suirokaku) and Sanmon gate; Tenjuan garden.
strings.d6.s3.name: Okutan Nanzenji Yudofu
strings.d6.s3.tips: Simmered tofu (yudofu) beside the temple; since 1635, quiet garden.
strings.d6.s4.name: Heian Shrine
strings.d6.s4.tips: Giant red torii; garden (weeping cherry in April).
strings.d6.b0.name: Blue Bottle Kyoto Nanzenji
strings.d6.b0.tips: Coffee in a machiya (townhouse); instead of tofu.
strings.d6.b1.name: Kyoto National Museum
strings.d6.b1.tips: National treasures; instead of Heian on a rainy day.
strings.d7.s0.name: Kamo River Morning Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: Riverbank; stepping stones between Sanjo and Shijo, herons.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pontocho Alley
strings.d7.s1.tips: Narrow geisha lane, quiet by day; kawayuka terraces in the evening (May to September).
strings.d7.s2.name: Kyoto Station Isetan
strings.d7.s2.tips: Depachika (basement food hall) inside the station and yatsuhashi souvenirs; rooftop Skyway is free.
strings.d7.s3.name: Kyoto Ramen Koji
strings.d7.s3.tips: Eight regional ramen shops on the station's 10th floor; a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s4.name: Kyoto Station Haruka Kansai
strings.d7.s4.tips: Haruka Express to Kansai takes 75 minutes; bus to Itami takes 55 minutes.
strings.d7.b0.name: Kyoto Tower Sando
strings.d7.b1.name: To-ji
strings.d7.b1.tips: Japan's tallest pagoda; next to the station, flea market on the 21st of the month.
strings.note0: Daily bus pass 700 JPY (tourist routes are packed), metro plus bus 1,100; ICOCA is the most practical. Haruka from Kansai takes 75 minutes; JR from Osaka takes 30 minutes. Bike rental 1,000 per day.
strings.note1: Maple foliage in late November (Tofuku-ji, Arashiyama, Eikando at night), cherry blossom in early April (Philosopher's Path, Maruyama); winter is 5°C, Kinkaku-ji under snow, January to February is quiet; March to May is crowded.
strings.note2: Temples cost 500-800 JPY, cash only; no eating while walking in Nishiki; private lanes in Gion have been off limits since 2024, do not stop maiko.
strings.note3: Yudofu, kaiseki (10,000+), obanzai (Kyoto home cooking), matcha; ramen 1,000, teishoku (set meal) 1,200; no tipping, cards are becoming common but carry cash.
strings.note4: Kiyomizu, Fushimi and the Bamboo Grove before 08:00; Kinkaku-ji and Nara open at 09:00; check Nijo's closing days.
strings.note5: Nara's deer eat paper and will bow; when the crackers are gone, show them your empty hands.
strings.transit.name: ICOCA + daily bus
strings.transit.why_chosen: Kyoto's bus network is extensive; the metro has only 2 lines; ICOCA works everywhere
